summary:
We developed TerraTwin, a web app that helps users find places on Earth that resemble landscapes on Mars or the Moon. Users upload a photo, and the app compares its visual features with 720 satellite images from 177 countries and areas. The closest matches appear as coloured flags on a 3D globe. Clicking a flag shows the Earth location beside the original photo and explains their similarities.
TerraTwin addresses the difficulty of finding Earth analogue sites—environments that can help researchers study planetary landscapes and plan equipment tests before space missions. We also developed a terrain dataset and machine-learning models to support terrain analysis.
The project makes planetary science more accessible to students, educators and researchers through real images and clear comparisons. Its results suggest candidate visual analogues, not exact locations or confirmed mission sites, providing a useful starting point for further investigation.
details: TerraTwin is a web app that helps people find places on Earth that look like landscapes on Mars or the Moon. Users upload a photo, and the app compares its colour, brightness, contrast and texture with 720 satellite images from 177 countries and areas. The closest matches appear as coloured flags on a 3D globe; clicking a flag shows the real place beside the uploaded photo and explains the similarities. We also built a terrain dataset and two machine-learning models to classify Earth landscapes and calculate terrain scores. We used TypeScript, React and Python, with tools such as Three.js and scikit-learn, while Manus helped with development and documentation. Its creative feature is combining real images, an interactive globe and clear explanations to make planetary science easier to explore. It can help students, teachers and researchers discover possible Earth analogue sites for study and equipment testing. Our team considered privacy, ease of use, data quality and differences between satellite and rover photos, so the app shows visual similarity—not an exact location or proof that a site is suitable for a mission.
